title: Nociceptors sense pathogens directly
objective: Explain evidence that nociceptors detect pathogens and modulate inflammation.

steps.title: Pain as an early warning
steps.body: **[[nociceptor|Nociceptors]]** can detect bacterial products directly — you feel pain from infection partly because the neurons sense the pathogen themselves. Strikingly, these neurons can then *modulate* the immune response, sometimes even dampening it.

steps.setup: In a skin infection, nociceptors are activated directly by bacteria. You then silence those nociceptors.
steps.prompt: What might happen to the local immune response?
options: It can change — sometimes increasing, since the neurons were modulating it
Nothing happens, since neurons have no effect on immunity at all
The bacteria would be cleared instantly without any neurons involved
It should simply weaken, since the pain signal normally recruits immune cells
steps.reveal: Chiu et al. found nociceptors sense bacteria and can *suppress* aspects of the immune response; silencing them changed infection outcomes. Neurons are active players, not bystanders.

options: Alter the local immune response they had been modulating
Have no possible effect on the immune response at all
Instantly sterilize the surrounding tissue on its own
variants.explanation: Nociceptors modulate immunity, so silencing them changes the response.

steps.prompt: What's the broader lesson from nociceptors sensing bacteria?
options: The nervous and immune systems are directly, physically interconnected
Only antibodies, never neurons, can ever possibly detect a pathogen at all
Pain is just a by-product of tissue damage, with no role in immunity
Neurons can detect pathogens but never actually affect them
steps.explanation: Direct pathogen sensing by neurons, plus their feedback onto immune cells, shows the two systems are wired together — the premise of neuroimmunology.

variants.setup: Neurons both detect bacteria and feed back on immune cells.
options: That pain is unrelated to infection
variants.reveal: It shows the nervous and immune systems are directly interconnected.

sources.note: Nociceptor neurons detect bacteria directly and modulate inflammation.
